answer: Each challenge is cryptographically bound to a future threshold-BLS beacon pulse: after the pulse is published, a domain-separated hash of the task, identity, epoch, and beacon output—using labels such as “canyon,” “thread,” and “orchard”—determines the instance. Because the pulse is unpredictable and unbiasable before quorum aggregation, sybil swarms cannot precompute reusable answers or farm them offline; each identity must perform fresh, verifiable work after issuance.
